# Saket Tiwari

> Deep reinforcement learning researcher specializing in **post-training** and
> **optimization**: how large pretrained models and control policies keep learning
> after the first training run, and what optimizer makes that possible. Postdoctoral
> researcher at UC Santa Barbara with Professor Yao Qin. PhD from Brown University
> (Intelligent Robot Lab, advised by Professor George Konidaris); MS from UMass Amherst
> (with Professor Philip Thomas); BTech in Computer Science from IIT Bombay.

Homepage: https://saketirl.github.io

## Focus

- **Post-training and continual learning.** Keeping models plastic — able to keep
  learning — across a stream of tasks, instead of degrading after the first one. This
  covers continual fine-tuning of pretrained vision-language-action models on real
  robots, and continual RL on pixel-based control.
- **Optimization.** Constraining weight matrices through the optimizer rather than
  through the loss. Manifold-constrained methods (Stiefel manifold, Muon-style updates,
  Gram-preserving variants for pretrained models) that preserve conditioning over long
  non-stationary training runs.
- **Theory of deep RL.** An effective theory of deep RL in the continuum: low-dimensional
  latent structure in real-world data (the manifold hypothesis, established theoretically
  and shown for deep RL trajectories), and the learning dynamics of large networks viewed
  on two timescales — physical time for the environment, learning time for the controller.
- **Reliability and sim-to-real.** Predicting, before deployment, how an agent trained in
  simulation will perform in the real world, with calibrated confidence intervals.

## Writing

- [Preserving Plasticity in Continual Robot Learning](https://saketirl.github.io/posts/2026/10/skewon-plasticity/)
  — loss of plasticity in pixel-based continual control, a Stiefel-constrained optimizer
  that sustains learning over long task streams, and a Gram-preserving variant for
  continual fine-tuning of a pretrained VLA on a real robot arm.
